answer: Each identity registers a vertex post with a 90-credit lantern bond. It files a lantern bearing to an observed plume, with flash time and vertex key. An auditor triangulates the plume origin from separate vertex bearings against a wind table; bearings missing the intersection, repeating a key, or reusing a lantern record burn the bond. Fee: first 36, kth 36+7(k-1), 1000th 7029; 1000 fakes pay 3,532,500 plus 90,000 locked. A rented-bearing ring fails: copied bearings cannot intersect at one plume point from distinct vertices. An honest agent pays 36 and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
